text: If your business email ends in at gmail dot com, you could be losing jobs before you even quote.
Here's why. Anyone can make a free Gmail with your business name in about two minutes.
So when a customer gets a quote from that address, they can't tell if it's really you, or a scammer pretending to be you.
Now compare that to jess at your business dot com dot au.
It matches your website, so it looks like a real, established business.
Only you can create addresses on your own domain, so a scammer can't just sign up for one.
And you don't have to give up the apps you already know.
Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 both let you use your own domain, right inside Gmail or Outlook.
One last tip. Ask whoever sets it up to turn on email authentication.
It tells inboxes your emails really came from you, so your quotes don't land in spam.
